message.content: {"rules":["An Allocator implementation must handle zero-sized allocations even if its underlying allocator does not support them or returns a null pointer for them.","A memory block is currently allocated by an allocator if its starting address was previously returned by that allocator's allocate, grow, or shrink method and the block has not subsequently been deallocated.","Calling deallocate deallocates the memory block. Calling grow or shrink deallocates the input memory block if it returns Ok, but does not deallocate that block if it returns Err.","Where an Allocator method requires a layout to fit a memory block, the block must be currently allocated with alignment layout.align(), and layout.size() must be in the inclusive range from the size of the layout used to allocate the block to the actual size returned by allocate, grow, or shrink.","Memory blocks currently allocated by an allocator must point to valid memory and retain their validity until the block is deallocated or the allocator is dropped.","Copying, cloning, or moving an allocator must not invalidate memory blocks returned from it.","A copied or cloned allocator must behave like the original allocator.","A currently allocated memory block may be passed to any method of its allocator that accepts such an argument."]}
